title: brain: theOS's memory, one schema, references pinned by commit
note: brain: the schema, the reflection and the trace of everything theOS keeps. It took AIP-1's memory parts (D-25).

questions.q: Is brain's direction right: a JSON doc per thing, JSON Lines for whatever only grows, a JSON Schema per type, binaries named by content hash, and every internal reference pinned as path@full commit SHA?
options: Yes, take it into AIP-3's Understand

questions.q: brain, two simplifications the review proposes against your direction (D-12, D-25): keep each list that only grows as a JSON array with a prefix check instead of JSON Lines, and compute a link's version from git (the commit that added the citing line) instead of storing path@SHA?
options: Both (recommended: no history was rewritten yet, and the static apps cannot read git objects)
Keep JSON Lines and stored pins, as decided

questions.q: AIP-3's link versions (c5): defer them until a correction is traced to a link whose target moved? Most links point at docs that never change or change all the time, so the flag would carry little signal, and showing it needs a publish step no AIP builds yet.
options: Defer c5 until such a correction (recommended)

questions.q: Gate A for AIP-3, after its spec review: are its claims, assumptions, outcome and mockup what must be true?

who: Samuel Andert, who must trust that the agents follow what he decided, as it stands now.
avenMAIA and its agents, which read brain before they act and write to it as they work.
Anyone who later asks why something is the way it is.
problem.experience: Decisions, words and history were kept in chat and in files edited in place: a newer decision did not say what it replaced, outdated words came back, and nobody could tell which step wrote what.

items.text: Decisions were listed oldest first, and a newer one did not say which older one it replaced (the dated decision docs, before D-15).
avenCEO had to be renamed by hand across 13 types, 25 terms and three apps, twice (D-17, D-21).
A read flag on 58 sources claimed a global truth that was per intent (D-22).
A link is a bare path, and the file behind it changes (D-12).

problem.baseline: Now: one JSON doc per thing in theOS/ (the counts are read off when Gate A is asked); the reflection and the trace computed by the apps; no schema, no check that history only grows, links by bare path.
whys: You can't be sure the agents follow what holds now. Why? Old and new decisions sat side by side, edited in place, without saying which replaces which.
Why? Memory had no rules: no schema per type, no history that only grows, no reflection, links that move.
Root cause: brain has no schema, and nothing enforces the reflection, the trace or the growth of history.
truths: Git keeps every version of every file; a commit SHA names exactly one.
What is computed from a log that only grows cannot drift from it.
A JSON Schema is checked by a program, without judgement.
Whether a new decision replaces an old one needs judgement: an agent proposes it, the decision records it.
assumptions: One JSON doc per thing stays fast enough for the apps at a few hundred docs.
Git history is never rewritten, so a version computed from git always resolves.
problem.risk: Can be undone: every change is files in git.

reuse.use: Used: the trace and the step are computed already; this AIP makes them enforced.

Learned from: records only grow, everything else is derived; content is addressed by its hash.

options.name: The direction you approved (D-25), simplified (D-31), for every type (D-32)
options.note: A JSON doc per thing; one reflection and one trace for every type; arrays that only grow, checked; a link's version computed from git; binaries by content hash when there are any.

options.name: A database
options.note: Rejected: git already versions, diffs and reviews files; a database would need its own history and review.

claims.promise: Every JSON doc in aip, decisions, sessions, sources, metrics, lessons, authors and avenCEO has a type with a type doc, and matches the JSON Schema inside it; by is always an author doc.
claims.fails: A misspelt field, a missing or misspelt type, or a free-text author passes unseen.
claims.check: Validated with ajv; each schema rejects a planted bad doc of its type; every current doc passes. Index docs and copied lists are checked separately (c8).

claims.promise: Every copied list (the index docs, the definition's lists, a session's decisions and intents) equals what it copies.
claims.fails: A list drifts, as session.intents did.
claims.check: The check compares each with its folder or backlinks.

claims.promise: A command lists what holds for every type, from the same holds() the apps use (ui/wiki.js), and theOS/CLAUDE.md names it as the first thing to read.
claims.fails: Agents act on a superseded doc because they read raw files.
claims.check: The command and the apps load one holds(); theOS/CLAUDE.md's first rule names the command.

claims.promise: One reflection for every type: what a new doc supersedes or merges ({doc, part, what}) held at the parent commit; what holds is computed, never stored.
claims.fails: A doc supersedes something that no longer held, or points at nothing.
claims.check: The check fails a planted supersedes of a doc already superseded at the parent, and a dangling path. Missed supersedes are caught by the outcome and the deferred checker, not here.

claims.promise: Every doc changed in a commit is written by an event added in that commit, by an author doc, in a step its type allows; an intent's own doc is covered by its new events. Metrics, lessons and every other doc are written only this way (D-40).
claims.fails: A doc changes that no AIP step wrote.
claims.check: The check fails a planted edit with no event, an event by a free string, and a measurement written outside a Learn step.

claims.promise: A term that renames a word carries the old word and where the rename applies, and the terms check fails when the old word comes back there, and stays quiet where its other meaning is right.
claims.fails: A rename sweep misses a place, or a word with two meanings raises a false alarm.
claims.check: A test plants each renamed word once where the rename applies and once where its other meaning is right; renames of avenCEO, aven and OLD-AIP are written as such term docs.

claims.promise: What only grows (an intent's events, a metric's measurements, a session's asks) stays a JSON array that only grows: a change that edits or drops an earlier entry fails.
claims.fails: History is rewritten and nothing notices.
claims.check: The check requires the base array to be a deep-equal prefix of the new one; a planted edit, deletion or rename of an old entry fails.

claims.promise: A link's version is computed, never stored: the version cited is the commit that added the citing line, and the check flags a link whose target changed since; the flag is written into the published artifact as one generated file, never committed.
claims.fails: A link silently shows content that changed after it was cited.
claims.check: A planted citation of a doc that changed after the citing commit is flagged, and the apps show the flag from the generated file.

outcome.promise: Over the three sessions after checkpoint 2: no correction whose cause is an outdated decision, an outdated word or a missed supersede.
outcome.how: Each correction event names its cause; counted per session.

checkpoints.adds: After AIP-1's checkpoint 1: schemas inside the type docs, validated with ajv; the single supersedes form; copied lists checked; holds() in ui/wiki.js and the command, named first in theOS/CLAUDE.md; the definition's rules and Reflection term updated; a cause field on corrections.
The reflection and the trace enforced on every commit.
Renames as term docs with their old word and scope; the terms check; AIP-1's sweep deleted from the done rule.
Arrays that only grow; a link's version, as you answer question 3.

deferred.what: The reflection run by a fresh checker, automatically
deferred.until: Three sessions without a correction whose cause is a missed supersede.

mockup: Every list in the Intents app, split into Hold now and Superseded: theOS/avenCEO/index.html#decisions, #terms, #lessons, #metrics
A link whose target changed since it was cited: a chip "changed since" beside it, opening the diff

source.text: Let's settle the schema of our single source of truth for everything we generate in AIPs, learnings and sources: what is a JSON file, what is a list of JSON entries, what is markdown, and what is both. And link every internal git resource by its commit hash, never by a bare file path, because history changes.
